title: EME Temple (Dakshinamurthy Temple), Vadodara - A Fusion of Faith and Modern Architecture
content:
EME Temple (Dakshinamurthy Temple), Vadodara

Located in the heart of Vadodara, the EME Temple, also known as the Dakshinamurthy Temple, is one of the city’s most unique and spiritually uplifting landmarks. Managed by the Indian Army, this temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and stands as a symbol of unity, peace, and modern architectural brilliance. Unlike traditional temples, the EME Temple is an extraordinary blend of spiritual devotion and futuristic design, attracting visitors from across India.

A Marvel of Modern Architecture

The EME Temple was constructed by the Electrical and Mechanical Engineering (EME) Corps of the Indian Army, which also explains its popular name. What sets this temple apart is its aluminum-clad geodesic structure, representing the universe and eternal cosmic energy.

The architectural design is deeply symbolic -

The dome represents the universe.

The spire symbolizes the holy Kalash (sacred pot).

The idol of Lord Shiva is placed beneath a beautiful glass canopy, highlighting simplicity and purity.

The temple’s design beautifully merges spiritual philosophy with modern engineering, making it a one-of-a-kind structure in India.

Spiritual and Cultural Harmony

Though primarily dedicated to Lord Shiva, the EME Temple also features symbols from five major religions - Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Buddhism, and Jainism - promoting interfaith unity and harmony. This inclusive representation makes the temple not only a religious site but also a message of universal brotherhood and peace.

Peaceful Ambiance and Visitor Experience

Surrounded by lush greenery, the temple complex offers a calm and meditative atmosphere. Visitors often describe the site as serene, disciplined, and well-maintained, thanks to the Indian Army’s management. The beautiful lawns, tall trees, and artistic sculptures around the temple enhance its tranquil charm, making it a perfect spot for reflection and spiritual rejuvenation.

Photography inside the temple premises is generally restricted for security reasons, but visitors can capture the exterior view and garden area.

Location

EME Temple, Fatehgunj, Vadodara, Gujarat - 390002
Located near the headquarters of the Indian Army’s Southern Command.

Timings

  • Monday to Sunday: 6:30 AM - 8:30 PM
  • Open all days of the week.

Entry Fee

  • Free entry for all visitors.
  • ID proof may be required for entry due to army security regulations.

How to Reach

  • By Air: Vadodara Airport is about 4 km away.
  • By Train: Vadodara Junction Railway Station is around 5 km away.
  • By Road: Easily accessible via local taxis, autos, and buses.
